note: Oracle for Stage 8 — the runnable effect link (issue #81). Hand-derived (R-CHAR-3) from .design/basis/08-runnable-effect-link.md. forge build emits `mod os { ... }` (the syscall-wrapper impls) into the generated crate, keyed by the reachable #[boundary("os::...")] targets, so a verified program that uses an effect primitive COMPILES + RUNS + does real I/O. forge check (verification) is UNCHANGED — the link is a build-only concern; the wrappers are the trusted-by-fiat, seccomp-confined, manifest-enumerated TCB. The mutation-floor 0 on elapsed_ok is the shape-only-effect-contract caveat (Stage 3): a timestamp bound is mutation-survivable, so the L3-to-boundary demo runs at floor 0.

verify_unchanged.name: now
verify_unchanged.why: now is the Time effect primitive -> L1 boundary (os::now, fx time). forge CHECK certifies it independent of the build link.

verify_unchanged.name: elapsed_ok
verify_unchanged.why: elapsed_ok calls now() (the boundary), ens result < 4_000_000_000 discharged through now's assumed ens -> L3, to-the-boundary via now (#52). forge check is unchanged by the runnable link.

build_and_run.name: elapsed_ok_runs
build_and_run.why: forge build --entry elapsed_ok emits `mod os { fn now() -> u64 { SystemTime::now()... } }`, rustc-links it (exit 0), and the binary RUNS -> prints elapsed_ok()'s result: a live Unix timestamp (a u64, > 0, < 4_000_000_000). This is THE unlock: a verified Thermite program runs + does real I/O (a clock_gettime syscall).

sandbox_confines.name: fx_time_allowlist
sandbox_confines.why: forge build --entry elapsed_ok derives an fx-time seccomp allowlist including clock_gettime (#57); the linked os::now's clock_gettime runs clean; a probe attempting an out-of-fx syscall (openat) under that filter -> SIGSYS-killed (exit 159). The linked wrapper is confined to its declared effect — a Time primitive cannot exceed Time syscalls.
